_comment: Two independent legs about the SAME code, composed by reference only -- neither tool knows the other exists. Built for yebiguo/ProofRun#12.

execution_binding_leg.source: ProofRun v0.3.0, local, offline, zero network calls
execution_binding_leg.claim: the declared 'test' check (pytest) actually ran against this exact commit and passed
execution_binding_leg.note: This says the 3 tests that exist all passed. It says nothing about whether those 3 tests are the right tests.

judgment_leg.claim: an independent reviewer's assessment of whether this code is safe/correct for its stated purpose
judgment_leg.note: This is a reputation-based judgment, signature-checkable (schnorr, offline, no trust in invinoveritas required to confirm WE issued it) but not re-derivable the way the test run is -- it found a real bug (negative max_fee_pct is never validated) that all 3 passing tests missed entirely.

why_both: The tests passing (execution-binding leg) and the code being safe (judgment leg) are two different claims. Here they actively disagree: 3/3 tests green, but the reviewer found a real negative-fee bug the tests never exercised. Composing both, unlinked at the tool level, surfaces that gap instead of hiding it behind a single green checkmark.
